items.title: Ed Polcer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: whether it was Benny Moten. Anyway, it looked at jazz from the influences on the music that was played at Eddie Condon’s.

ctx.x: This concept of “The Magic of Swing Street,” when did it kind of come together for you?

Well Community — Columbia Artists came to a concert I did in 1992 up at the Emelin Theater up in Westchester. I invited them because I knew that they have probably five or six hundred venues throughout the United States, an organization called Community Concerts. And what they do is, it started out as a classical Columbia Records or Columbia Recordings started it many years ago, 75 or 80 years ago, as an outlet for their artists and what they did was a small community would get up a budget let’s say of $30,000…

Night at Eddie Condon’s.” And we toured for three -- two years with that. And we must have hit maybe 120 different concerts just doing that. And I went to the people at Columbia Artists and said I’d like another go-around and I’ve got a great idea for another show that we could do and they came up with the title, “The Magic of Swing Street.” I said you know we could show going beyond what — “A Night at Eddie Condon’s” described what went on at Eddie Condon’s and it showed the influences of all the influences…
